To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{{\left(y+2\right)}^{2}} \\ {\left(y+2\right)}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {\left(y+2\right)}^{2}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\ \int {\left(y+2\right)}^{2}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\ \int {\left(y+2\right)}^{2}\,\text{d}y & =\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{{\left(y+2\right)}^{3}}{3} & =\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+K \\ {\left(y+2\right)}^{3} & ={x}^{3}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=3K.$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
{\left(y+2\right)}^{3}={x}^{3}+C.
$$
